completion_data.completion_summary: Added a per-type (removed<=added) artifact-loss invariant as a new FAIL-level D5 check in validate-state.sh --deep, reusing D4's git-diff mechanism, with a repeatable --allow-artifact-removal CLI opt-in, six bidirectional fixture tests proving both rejection and opt-in acceptance on a raw jq-composed write, an explicit append-only rule in rules/state-management.md, and a new MUST NOT bullet in general-implementation-agent.md.

memory_candidates.content: When adding a machine-checkable append-only invariant over an array field whose sanctioned writers use a 'remove-same-type-then-add-one' idiom (a common jq pattern for 'latest pointer' fields like state.json's artifacts list), design the invariant as a per-key COUNT rule (removed(K) <= added(K) for each distinct key K, e.g. an artifact 'type'), never a strict path/element superset rule. A superset rule breaks every routine sanctioned supersession call; the count rule is a no-op for first-writes, permits 1-for-1 supersession, and still catches bulk/silent loss shaped like the original incident.

A test suite whose validator-resolution prefers the deployed copy over the source-store copy (to test 'what's actually live') creates a false-green risk for brand-new checks added to the source store but not yet deployed: the new fixtures would silently run against a stale deployed binary that lacks the check. Fix: give new fixtures for a not-yet-deployed feature their OWN validator-candidate list ordered source-store-first, and grep each candidate for a stable identifier string (e.g. a code comment like 'Check D5') before trusting it -- loudly info-skip if no candidate qualifies. This lets the new fixtures genuinely execute pre-deploy while never risking a false pass against stale code.

Scripts under agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/ that shell out to sibling scripts via a hardcoded '../..'-relative repo-root guess (e.g. generate-todo.sh) can refuse to run when invoked directly from the source-store tree instead of the deployed .claude/ tree, producing an unrelated-looking FAIL (e.g. a TODO.md sync check failure) that has nothing to do with the feature under test. Before concluding a new check is broken, verify the same failure reproduces on the unmodified script (e.g. via git stash) from the same invocation path -- it may be a pre-existing source-store-vs-deployed-tree limitation, not a regression.
